data.turoyo: E umarno: “D šəqlitu u fəlim mene, annaqqe i naqqayo gəd milakhitu bə ḥḏo naqqa!“
data.translation: Yes, I am saying: ‘If you take the film from him, then at that very moment you will ruin it completely!’

rationale: Fills the thin II Infectum sense-1 cell with a material participant contrasting with the inherited reputational example; complete condition supplies the film antecedent.

summary: Collective u ʕamo occurs with a singular-shaped Infectum and a first-person affected participant. The moral evaluation and following mockery support reputational staining without requiring an overt honour noun.
No new form, Detransitive use or Idiomatic phrases is supplied; the existing example already establishes the figurative use.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English quotations below retain the supplied project machine translation and are marked as such; sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Where available, round-1 proposals are retained in the human layout and counts, and are not resubmitted in this JSON.

The written narrative combines gəd with second-plural Infectum milakhitu, whose i-vowel differs from the inherited base mlakəh. Preserve the attested spelling; a single token does not establish a separate paradigm.

The threatened damage follows taking the film from the camera owner. The verb is a full predicate here, without a light-verb noun construction. Do not turn the camera scenario into an etymological or photographic-mechanism claim.

Targeted permitted glossary searches: mlakh gives only the inherited lkh Part. Pass.; milakh has no hit. The naqq search gives i=naqq-ayo in ʔṯy and ʕmṣ examples, supporting the temporal reading of i naqqayo.

Does milakhitu here specifically mean staining or fogging the film, or broader spoiling? The supplied Turoyo and machine English do not determine the physical mechanism; confirm with a speaker before adding a technical sense.
Der vorhandene Beleg befleckt den Ruf einer Person: -li bezeichnet die betroffene Person; eine eigene Nominalphrase „Ehre“ steht nicht im Turoyo.
Photographischer Film als aus dem Vordersatz erschlossener betroffener Gegenstand; die genaue Beschädigung bleibt offen, insbesondere ist Lichteinwirkung nicht ausdrücklich genannt.
